request: I run a small provisions shop in Madina and I want to keep my price list on the computer instead of in my notebook. I want to add the things I sell with their prices. I want to see everything I sell, and look up the price of one thing. Sometimes I stop selling something, so I want to take it off the list.
summary:
I've built your shop's price list program, and all 13 of my checks pass. Your items are saved in a file called `shop.db` in the same folder as the program.

Every item has an item number (given automatically), a name, a price in cedis and pesewas, and the date it was added (filled in automatically).

**What you can do**
- **POST /items**: add an item by giving its name and price, for example `{"name": "Milo tin", "price": 30.00}`. It's saved with its item number and today's date.
- **GET /items**: see your whole price list.
- **GET /items/{itemNumber}**: look up the name and price of one item.
- **DELETE /items/{itemNumber}**: take an item off the list. After that it no longer shows up, and you can add it again later if you start selling it again.

**What gets refused**
- An item with no name, or a name that is only spaces.
- An item with no price.
- A negative price, or a price written in words like "twelve". The price also has to be typed as a plain number: `12.50` works, but `"12.50"` in quotation marks is refused.
- A price with more than two digits after the decimal point, like 12.555.
- A name that's already on the list, even with different capital letters. If "Sugar" is there, "sugar" is refused.
- Looking up or removing an item number that isn't on the list. You get a message saying it was not found, and nothing changes.

As agreed, you can't change the price of an item that's already on the list. For now, you'd remove it and add it again with the new price, which gives it a new item number and date. We can add proper price changes later if you want.

plan.summary: This plan sets up a simple price list for your provisions shop in Madina, so you can keep it on the computer instead of in your notebook. You will be able to add an item you sell with its price, see the full list of everything you sell, look up the price of one item, and remove an item when you stop selling it. Nothing in your request was unsafe or outside the price list, so nothing was left out. Changing the price of an item that is already on the list was not part of your request, so it is not included here. If you want that, we can add it before anything is built.

data.name: Item
fields: Item number: a number the system gives each item automatically so it can tell items apart
Name: what the item is called, for example 'Rice 5kg bag' or 'Milo tin'
Price: how much you sell it for, in cedis and pesewas
Date added: the day the item was put on the list, filled in automatically

endpoints.does: Adds a new item to your price list. You give the item's name and its price, and it is saved.
Shows your whole price list: every item you sell, with its price.
Shows the name and price of one item, so you can quickly check what it costs.
Takes an item off your price list when you stop selling it. Once it is removed, it no longer appears in the list.

rules: An item cannot be added without a name.
An item cannot be added without a price.
The price must be a number that is zero or more. A negative price, or a price written in words, will be refused.
The price can have at most two digits after the decimal point, for example 12.50 cedis. A price like 12.555 will be refused.

Two items with the same name cannot be on the list at the same time, so you never have two different prices for the same thing. Capital letters do not count as a difference, so 'Sugar' and 'sugar' are treated as the same name.
If you look up or remove an item that is not on the list, you will get a clear message saying it was not found, and nothing will change.
